entries.summary: The Sun Yat-sen profile used corrupted birth, death, and birthplace claims from a pinned upstream revision.
entries.before: The profile said Sun Yat-sen was born in the Soviet Union on 12 November 1956 and died in 2025, then computed a chart from those values.
entries.after: The reviewed record now uses 12 November 1866 in Cuiheng, China, and 12 March 1925, supported by the Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hall. The birth time remains unknown, so the chart uses the documented noon-reference convention and omits houses and angles. The original upstream snapshot remains pinned for audit, while a Git-reviewed authoritative override controls publication.

entries.summary: The Roberto Clemente profile used Italy and its country centroid as his birthplace.
entries.before: The profile described Roberto Clemente as born in Italy and computed the noon-reference chart in the Europe/Rome time zone.
entries.after: The reviewed record now uses Carolina, Puerto Rico, supported independently by Major League Baseball and the National Baseball Hall of Fame. The chart was recomputed in America/Puerto_Rico. The birth time remains unknown, so houses and angles are still omitted.

entries.summary: A People profile stated a settled Sun sign for a birth date on which the Sun changed sign.
entries.before: The profile for B. F. Skinner, born 20 March 1904, presented his Sun as settled in Pisces at 29.7°, and the directory filed him under Pisces — while the page’s own transitions note said the sign was left open.
entries.after: The profile has been withdrawn. The Sun crossed from Pisces into Aries during that day at the birthplace, and with no recorded birth time his Sun sign cannot be determined, so no sign should have been published. The determinability test compared the UTC day rather than the birthplace’s own civil day, which can differ by up to twelve hours; it now measures the civil day, and a new gate fails any record whose stated Sun sign contradicts its own recorded transitions. No other profile was affected.
